title: Ascentor POC Security Workshop - Evidence & Response Binder
body:
Executive summary:

This binder captures the security and compliance artifacts, questionnaire responses, and workshop notes produced during the Ascentor Financial POC (week of 2025-11-03). Purpose: provide a single-reference evidence pack for Ascentor security reviewers and internal audit leads to validate Redwood Private deployment controls and residual action items from the workshop.

POC scope and constraints:
- Customer: Ascentor Financial (payments platform prototype)
- Deployment mode: Redwood Private (VPC-hosted control plane, customer-managed data plane)
- Focus areas: network segmentation, key management, data residency, audit logging, and incident response
- Timebox: 3-week technical POC + 1 workshop day for security deep-dive
- Out of scope: full SOC2 audit, production SLA commitments (these are follow-ups if POC proceeds)

Summary of findings (high level):
- Network controls: VPC peering and transit gateway design accepted; customer requested an extra NAT gateway for analytics cluster to enforce egress policies.
- Key management: HSM-backed KMS integration validated; proof of key rotation and split access demonstrated.
- Logging & monitoring: We provided sample CloudWatch/ELK exports and a retention policy draft; Ascentor asked for 13 months retention (we currently keep 12 by default — action to update retention config for the POC cluster).
- Data residency: Deployment placed in eu-west-1 per request; region-specific backups confirmed.
- Least privilege: RBAC mapping documented; minor role consolidation recommended.

Evidence inventory (mapping questionnaire items to artifacts):
- Q1: Encryption at rest (Customer Q#2) -> evidence: kms-hsm-integration-screenshots.pdf; kms-rotation-demo.mp4
- Q2: Network segmentation (Customer Q#7) -> evidence: vpc-architecture-diagram.png; segmentation-test-results.csv
- Q3: Access control & least privilege (Customer Q#4) -> evidence: iam-role-matrix.csv; sprint-pr-roles-apply.patch
- Q4: Audit logging & retention (Customer Q#9) -> evidence: logging-retention-policy-draft.docx; sample-logs-2025-11-05.json
- Q5: Incident response (Customer Q#12) -> evidence: ir-runbook-excerpt.md; tabletop-notes-2025-11-06.txt
- Q6: Third-party dependencies (Customer Q#15) -> evidence: third-party-vendor-list.csv; sbom-snapshot-2025-10-28.json

Workshop notes (2025-11-06 security deep-dive):
- Attendees: Ascentor security lead (Priya Nair), Ascentor infra lead (Markus Bjorn), Redwood SEs (Aisha, Miguel), Solutions Eng PM (Rina), SRE contact (Tom)
- Opening: 15-minute runthrough of architecture and threat model assumptions.
- Demonstrations delivered:
  - Live KMS HSM rotation and audit trail (Aisha): showed key rotation, split access controls, and signed key metadata.
  - VPC isolation tests (Tom): executed simulated lateral-movement tests between model-serving nodes and analytics cluster; results attached.
  - Logging pipeline sample queries (Miguel): demonstrated alert for anomalous token-volume spikes.
- Raised issues and clarifications:
  - Ascentor requested explicit proof of cross-region failover without sending logs across borders. Action: provide region-isolation test script.
  - Clarify retention policy exception handling for legal holds. Action: draft exception workflow and owner.

Outstanding action items (owner and target dates):
- Update logging retention for POC cluster to 13 months (Owner: Miguel Alvarez, Due: 2025-11-14)
- Provide region-isolation test script showing no cross-region log egress (Owner: Tom Keenan, Due: 2025-11-13)
- Deliver formal keyed HSM architecture diagram with split-control annotations (Owner: Aisha Mbaye, Due: 2025-11-10)
- Create RBAC consolidation proposal and minimal-privilege mapping (Owner: Rina Sato, Due: 2025-11-16)
- Prepare legal-hold exception workflow and contact points (Owner: Danielle Cho, Due: 2025-11-18)

Risk register (selected):
- Risk: Log retention mismatches may fail customer policy; Mitigation: temporary config override for POC and follow-up engineering change if contract proceeds.
- Risk: Audit evidence produces PII traces in sample logs; Mitigation: scrubber applied to all shared samples and a documented scrubbing process included in this binder.

Evidence sharing notes and redaction policy:
- All sample logs in this bundle have been sanitized (PII redaction token: <REDACTED>). Original artifacts remain in the secure customer sandbox and were not exported.
- When exporting artifacts to Ascentor reviewers, use presigned links with 7-day expiry and require SSO access.

Appendix: Selected artifact descriptions (what to expect in each file)
- kms-hsm-integration-screenshots.pdf -> Annotated screenshots of HSM console showing key creation, rotation schedule, and access policies.
- vpc-architecture-diagram.png -> Network diagram illustrating subnet placement, NAT gateways, and security group boundaries used during POC.
- segmentation-test-results.csv -> Results of connectivity tests: expected-deny vs observed-allow, timestamps, and test harness commands.
- iam-role-matrix.csv -> CSV mapping of personas to roles and minimum permissions, plus justification notes.
- logging-retention-policy-draft.docx -> Draft policy for retention/archival with suggested retention periods and legal-hold procedure stub.

Recommended next steps (for the customer):
1) Accept the 13-month retention override for the POC and confirm in writing to unblock evidence review.
2) Approve a one-week extension for the POC if a region-isolation test is required across multiple availability zones.
3) Schedule a follow-up tabletop IR drill with Ascentor incident responders and Redwood on-call SREs.

Contact list (Redwood POC):
- Aisha Mbaye, Solutions Engineer, aisha@redwood.ai, +1-415-555-0182
- Miguel Alvarez, Senior SE (Networking), miguel@redwood.ai
- Rina Sato, Solutions PM, rina@redwood.ai
- Tom Keenan, SRE Lead, tom@redwood.ai

Document history and provenance:
- 2025-11-02: initial draft prepared after first deployment run (Aisha)
- 2025-11-06: workshop additions (notes and evidence list)
- 2025-11-10: added HSM architecture diagram link and clarified RBAC recommendations
- 2025-11-12: current revision; sent to Ascentor security mailing list for preliminary review

Distribution instructions:
- Internal: tag as POC-ASNT-2025 in Confluence and link to JIRA-POC-4882.
- External to customer: export only artifacts listed in the Evidence inventory section, use redaction script prior to sharing, and deliver via presigned links with access-limited SSO.

Notes to reviewers:
- This binder is intentionally scoped to POC evidence. If Ascentor requests production-grade compliance artifacts (SOC2, ISO, FedRAMP), we will transition to the enterprise onboarding playbook and collect additional continuous controls evidence.

End of binder.
